lessons.unit: Unit 1: Relationships and the online world
lessons.title: Belonging and friendship: healthy and unhealthy relationships
objectives: Describe the features of a healthy friendship
Recognise signs of an unhealthy or controlling relationship
Use respectful strategies to build and repair friendships, including online

keywords.def: a limit that shows what you are comfortable with
treating others as valuable and listening to them
understanding how someone else feels
people of a similar age you spend time with
good manners and character

starter: Bismillah. Name three qualities of a good friend.
What is the difference between a disagreement and bullying?
Give one example of a trusted adult.

teach.heading: What makes a relationship healthy?
teach.note: Say bismillah. Welcome pupils to Key Stage 3 PSHE and set ground rules. Ask pupils to list the people they have relationships with: family, friends, classmates, teachers, online groups. Draw out features of healthy relationships. Link to the hadith that none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself (Bukhari and Muslim). Link to the Tarbiyyah Compass values of Integrity and Excellence (adab). Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Anonymous questions can go to the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Warning signs of unhealthy relationships
bullets: Controlling who you see or talk to
Pressure to do things you do not want
Making you feel guilty or afraid
teach.note: Present invented examples: a friend checks your phone and gets angry about who you message; a group laughs at someone and says it is ‘just banter’. Ask pupils to rate each example: healthy, worrying or unsafe. Teach that unhealthy relationships are not always obvious at first. Emphasise that pupils are never to blame and that they can ask for support at any time.

teach.heading: Boundaries and respect
bullets: Boundaries are personal and different for everyone
You can say no, and so can others
teach.note: Practise assertive phrases: ‘I'd rather not.’ ‘That makes me uncomfortable.’ ‘Please stop.’ Teach that respecting another person's no is part of adab. Give examples about borrowing belongings, sharing secrets, sharing photos and personal space. Misconception: if someone does not say no loudly, it is fine to continue. Teach that we should stop when someone seems unsure.

teach.heading: Making and keeping friends in an online school
bullets: Be kind in chats and on camera
Keep group chats welcoming and inclusive
Ask an adult if a friendship worries you
teach.note: TGA pupils meet online, so friendship needs extra effort. Discuss netiquette: respond kindly, do not leave people out of group tasks, do not take screenshots to mock others, and follow the Behaviour and Online Conduct Policy. Ask: ‘What can you do this week to welcome someone new?’ Link to the Tarbiyyah Compass value of Excellence.

teach.heading: Choosing good company
bullets: Choose friends who help you do good
Hadith: a person follows the way of his close friend
Repair friendships with honesty and apology
teach.note: Cite plainly: the Prophet (peace be upon him) said that a person is on the way of his close friend, so let each of you look at whom he takes as a friend (Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi). Discuss: ‘How can friends make us better?’ Teach a repair sequence: calm down, say sorry for your part, listen, agree what will change. Link to forgiveness.

practice: Sort into healthy, worrying or unsafe: (a) a friend shares your homework tips (b) a friend tells you not to talk to anyone else (c) a friend always borrows things without asking.
Write one assertive sentence you could use to refuse something you are uncomfortable with.
List two ways to make a new classmate feel welcome in an online lesson.
independent: Write a short scenario showing a warning sign in a friendship and how the person responds.
Create a ‘Friendship charter’ with five promises for your class.
Write a paragraph explaining how choosing good company supports Eeman and Integrity.
exit: Name two features of a healthy relationship.
Give one warning sign of an unhealthy relationship.
lessons.homework: Write down three qualities you bring to a friendship and one way you can improve as a friend.
lessons.send: SEND: use scenario cards with traffic-light sorting. EAL: provide key phrase cards for assertive responses. Stretch: research how the Prophet (peace be upon him) treated his companions and link three examples to friendship qualities.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Relationships and the online world
lessons.title: Social media, gaming and your digital footprint
objectives: Explain how to protect privacy and reputation online
Describe risks of group chats, gaming and social media and how to respond
Know how and where to report online concerns

keywords.def: the trail of information left by your online activity
a control that limits who sees your content
an image of what is on a screen, often shared
what other people think of you
to tell the platform or a trusted adult about a problem

starter: Bismillah. What is a digital footprint?
Give two examples of personal information to keep private.
What are the steps of Stop, Block, Tell?

teach.heading: Our online lives
bullets: We use apps, games and group chats
Most social media sets a minimum age of 13
teach.note: Say bismillah. Begin with a quick poll: which types of apps do pupils use? Do not ask for names of accounts. Explain that age limits are set by platforms and linked to data and safety rules. Ask: ‘What are the good things about being online?’ Then introduce the risks. Link to the Tarbiyyah Compass value of Contentment: using technology in a balanced and grateful way. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Anonymous questions can go to the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Footprint and reputation
bullets: Posts, likes and comments can last
Others can copy, share and screenshot
Future schools and employers may look
teach.note: Explain that deleting does not always remove copies. Use an invented example: a joke message from Year 7 resurfaces in Year 11. Ask: ‘Would you be proud if your parents, teachers and a future employer saw this?’ Cite plainly: the Prophet (peace be upon him) said that whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent (Bukhari and Muslim). Apply it to typing.

teach.heading: Privacy and settings
bullets: Set accounts to private where possible
Accept only people you know in real life
teach.note: Walk through a mock privacy menu on screen. Teach the three-random-words password method and two-step verification. Explain that sharing passwords with friends, even trusted ones, can lead to hacked accounts and conflicts. Ask: ‘Why might an online friend not be who they say they are?’ Ensure pupils know that they should not meet online contacts.

teach.heading: Group chats and gaming
bullets: Never share photos of others without consent
Mute, block and leave if chat turns nasty
teach.note: Present an invented case: a group chat starts mocking a pupil's accent. Ask: ‘What are the options? What takes courage?’ Link to Qur'an 49:11 on not mocking others and 49:12 on avoiding backbiting. Mention that in-game purchases and loot boxes are designed to encourage spending, and that pupils should check with a parent before spending. Cyberbullying can be reported under the Anti-Bullying and Cyberbullying Policy.

teach.heading: How to report and get help
bullets: Block and report in the app
Save evidence, then tell a trusted adult
Report to the DSL at TGA
teach.note: Make sure all pupils know exactly who to tell at TGA. Explain that nobody will be punished for reporting in good faith. Introduce Report Remove, a tool from Childline and the Internet Watch Foundation that helps under-18s ask for nude or sexual images of themselves to be taken down. Keep this factual and brief; Y9 explores it further. Remind pupils that help is available without blame.

practice: Rewrite this post so it is kinder and safer: ‘Look where I am right now at Elmwood Park, come and find me!’
A friend sends you a screenshot mocking another pupil. List three possible responses and choose the best.
True or false? (a) Deleting a post always removes all copies. (b) Most social media platforms set a minimum age of 13. (c) You should accept any request from someone in your game.
independent: Create an infographic with five rules for a safe and positive digital footprint.
Role-play in pairs: one pupil is invited into a nasty group chat and the other helps them respond.
Write a letter to a friend explaining how to set up privacy settings and why.
exit: Give two reasons to be careful about what you post.
Name two places to report an online problem.
lessons.homework: Review the privacy settings on one account you use, with a parent or carer, and write three sentences on what you changed.
lessons.send: SEND: use a step-by-step visual checklist. EAL: pre-teach digital vocabulary with screenshots. Stretch: research the Online Safety Act 2023 and summarise how it protects children.

lessons.bigQuestion: Is all stress bad? Can a little stress ever help?
objectives: To understand what stress is and how to manage it with healthy strategies

hook.text: Is all stress bad? Can a little stress ever help?
hook.a: A little can help us focus (before a test); too much for too long harms.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear' (al-Baqarah 2:286) and 'Verily, with hardship comes ease' (ash-Sharh 94:5-6). Tawakkul means doing our part, then trusting Allah with the outcome.

hook.text: Teenagers often feel awake late at night. Is that laziness or biology?

islamicLink.text: Allah says He made the night as a covering and sleep as rest (al-Furqan 25:47). The Prophet ﷺ disliked sleeping before Isha and talking after it (al-Bukhari). An early night helps us wake for Fajr.

lessons.title: First aid basics: the first aid kit and calling for help
lessons.bigQuestion: A younger sibling burns their hand on a hot pan. What should happen in the next 20 minutes?
objectives: To understand how to call for help in an emergency and use a first aid kit for minor injuries safely
successCriteria: All: say when and how to call 999

hook.text: A younger sibling burns their hand on a hot pan. What should happen in the next 20 minutes?
hook.a: Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes, remove anything tight nearby, cover loosely, get an adult, and seek medical help if needed (NHS guidance).

islamicLink.text: Allah praises saving a life: 'whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely' (Al-Ma'idah 5:32). Learning first aid is a way to help others.
